source_problem: Salez arXiv:2508.21055 Problem 2.3: prove that all vertex-transitive expanders exhibit cutoff

new_class.name: C3 rotating-lamp semidirect Cayley lifts of degree-six Ramanujan Cayley graphs
new_class.input: L_n = Cay(K_n,U_n), |U_n|=6, Ramanujan; C3 cyclically permutes three copies of K_n
new_class.long_range_expansion: fails every fixed positive LRE constant; singleton-ball ratio at r=floor((1/2)log_7 N) is N^{-beta+o(1)}, beta=(1/2)(1-log_7 5)>0

mechanism_advance.previous_obstruction: the 10:30 normalizing-voltage theorem required monodromy to normalize the hidden generator set; nonnormalizing monodromy was left as the next structural obstruction
mechanism_advance.removed_scope: a nonnormalizing phase can rotate one vertical generator set through three disjoint coordinate copies and still preserve cutoff
mechanism_advance.key_identity: conditional on the C3 phase path, the three lamp coordinates are independent source-continuous-time walks with operational times B_j(t)=(6/8) A_j(t), where A_j is phase occupation time
mechanism_advance.concentration: A_j(t)=t/3+O_P(sqrt(t)); an explicit Poisson-equation martingale gives second moment O(t)
mechanism_advance.reason_normalizer_is_unnecessary_here: the three conjugate vertical semigroups commute because they act on distinct direct-product coordinates

remaining_obstruction: arbitrary transitive spectral expanders need not admit a finite switching representation with commuting conjugate semigroups or any sharp macroscopic factor; genuinely noncommuting monodromy remains unresolved
partner_complement: P26 remains on shell entropy/Green/spherical-distance transfer, most recently all fixed exact distances on EFMP biregular Cayley bigraphs
failed_or_preserved_routes: raw NBRW trace necessity remains ruled out by prior NM13-01 work
no claim that finite numerical checks prove the asymptotic theorem
